tier_reason: The only numbers are in the authors' own ACL 2016 demo paper (P16-4016), which could not be opened here (aclanthology.org and preview.aclanthology.org do not resolve; liner.com and lacuna review pages also blocked); WebSearch snippets corroborate the Gov2 (MeTA 1h12m vs Indri over 8h), 20news (80.1% in 0.648 s vs LIBLINEAR 79.4% in 2.58 s) and Webspam (99.4% in 1m16s, LIBLINEAR and SVMmulticlass fail on memory) figures, but no benchmark code, hardware, compiler or baseline versions are public. A peer-reviewed paper could support B once its tables are read; snippet-only evidence stays at C.

corrections.license: MIT OR NCSA (repo carries LICENSE.mit and LICENSE.ncsa, both copyright 2016 Sean Massung and Chase Geigle; neither file states how they combine; both OSI-approved)
corrections.claimed_speedup: Snippet only (paper unreachable). Indexing, Blog06: MeTA 11m 23s vs Lucene 20m 23s vs Indri 55m 40s (about 1.8x vs Lucene, 4.9x vs Indri, derived from snippet data; these Blog06 and Lucene figures come only from the search agent's garbled snippet and were not corroborated by this verifier's searches). Gov2 (147 GB, 25.2M docs): MeTA 1h 12m 10s vs Lucene 1h 59m 42s vs Indri 8h 13m 43s (about 1.7x vs Lucene and 6.8x vs Indri, derived from snippet data; a second summary corroborates MeTA 1h12m vs Indri over eight hours). Classification, 20news: MeTA 80.1% accuracy in 0.648 s vs LIBLINEAR 79.4% in 2.58 s (about 4x, derived from snippet data; timing covers training plus testing and excludes IO). Webspam: MeTA 99.4% accuracy in 1m 16s; LIBLINEAR and SVMmulticlass could not run for lack of memory (a capability result, not a speed ratio).
corrections.caveats: Snippet only: aclanthology.org, preview.aclanthology.org, liner.com, lacuna.tiptreesystems.com and edutechwiki were unreachable, so the paper's tables were never opened by search agent or verifier; the Blog06/Lucene indexing figures rest on one garbled WebSearch extract, while the Gov2-vs-Indri, 20news and Webspam figures are corroborated by a second snippet source. The numbers are first-party (the MeTA authors' ACL 2016 demo paper); hardware, compiler, flags, Lucene/Indri/LIBLINEAR versions and query-speed results are unknown (one summary says retrieval performance across the three systems was roughly even; index sizes comparable, Lucene 2.06 GB vs MeTA 2.84 GB on Blog06 and 11.02 GB vs 10.24 GB on Gov2). The repo carries no benchmark code; the website's online-learning tutorial only says LIBLINEAR is killed while loading the 1.2 GB Webspam training set, whereas MeTA's online SGD runs in 128 MB RSS. Filed under autodiff-and-ml-kernels, but none of that category's baselines (oneDNN, cuDNN, XNNPACK, Eigen tensor) are compared; MeTA is a text-retrieval/indexing and text-classification toolkit, which fits text-search-and-indexing better. Last commit on master 2017-08-20 (hotfix-v3.0.2 merge); the develop branch was last touched 2018-12-16 (CI/build bumps); abandoned either way.

notes: Real, peer-reviewed toolkit (719 stars, 240 forks) whose speed claims could not be checked against the PDF because every ACL Anthology host is blocked here; the Gov2/Indri, 20news and Webspam numbers are corroborated by independent snippets, the Blog06/Lucene numbers are not. Shortcomings: first-party numbers, no public benchmark harness or methodology, baselines not in list, wrong category (better text-search-and-indexing), abandoned since 2017-2018; a paper-access retier could lift it to B.

tier_reason: README FFT table (CUDA + cuFFT 0.1792 ms, MatX cudaExecutor 0.1848 ms, MatX CUDAJITExecutor 0.1114 ms = 1.61x) comes from the public harness examples/fft_benchmark.cu (interleaved trials, 10 warmups, 2000 iterations x 7 trials, median, outputs validated against the cuFFT reference at 2e-3 relative tolerance), with CUDA 13.0 + MathDx 26.03, a stated Release CMake configure (flags in the public CMakeLists.txt) and the DGX Spark GB10 GPU plus its named 20-core Arm CPU. Host compiler version is not stated, but the timed work is device code built by the named nvcc.

corrections.caveats: First-party NVIDIA numbers on one machine (DGX Spark GB10); the README says performance depends on GPU, clocks, shape and software versions. The FFT baseline is a 59-line handwritten CUDA + cuFFT pipeline written by the MatX authors (separate normalize kernel, out-of-place cufftExecC2C, separate calibrate/magnitude/dB kernel, two cudaMalloc temporaries); the plain cudaExecutor path is 3% slower than it, so the 1.61x comes only from fusing pre- and post-processing into one cuFFTDx kernel via CUDAJITExecutor, not from a faster FFT. The baseline does not use cuFFT's own load/store (LTO) callbacks, the incumbent's native way to fuse such pre/post work, so the gap against a best-practice cuFFT pipeline is unmeasured. JIT compile time is reported separately and excluded from steady-state timing. No comparison against the fft category's baselines (FFTW, MKL FFT, KissFFT): the harness can print an optional MatX host result through NVPL or FFTW, but the README publishes none. Black-Scholes rows (off-category, tier C on their own): the reproduce command omits CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE, which in MatX's CMakeLists adds -lineinfo and leaves host flags unoptimized (device code still gets nvcc's default optimization); examples/black_scholes.cu prints four MatX variants (plain expression, custom operator, apply() lambda, apply_idx() lambda) with no warmup before the first, and the README does not say which row gives 16.07 ms (the Python companion's docstring says it matches the apply() case); MatX inputs are unclamped uniform [0,1) while the Python harness clamps to 1e-6; MatX is timed by CUDA events in C++ and CuPy/NumPy by a separate Python script; the CuPy baseline is an eager expression with materialized intermediates, not a fused cupy.fuse or ElementwiseKernel; NumPy/SciPy runs single-threaded on the CPU, so 184.5x compares a GPU with one CPU thread. The README FFT benchmark was added on 2026-07-22 (#1208).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: CUDA 13.0 (nvcc) with MathDx 26.03 for the JIT case; FFT reproduce command: cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DMATX_BUILD_EXAMPLES=ON -DMATX_EN_MATHDX=ON, cmake --build build --target fft_benchmark, ./build/examples/fft_benchmark 256 4096 2000 (CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES defaults to native; MATX_CUDA_FLAGS adds --threads 0 --extended-lambda). The Black-Scholes reproduce command omits CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE (MatX then adds -lineinfo). Host C++ compiler and version not stated.

notes: Numbers match the README exactly and come from a public, validated, interleaved harness, so A stands for the FFT pipeline; the Black-Scholes rows are a weaker, off-category comparison (unfused CuPy, single-thread NumPy, ambiguous MatX row). Shortcomings: baseline written by the MatX authors and not using cuFFT callbacks, speedup comes from kernel fusion via cuFFTDx rather than a faster FFT, cudaExecutor alone is 3% slower than handwritten CUDA + cuFFT, single machine (GB10), no FFTW/MKL/KissFFT comparison; experimental JIT fusion rejects unsupported shapes.
